title: The channel protocol carries agent identity, updates and ending
body:
A socket client reports `{"status": {"state": …, "message": …}}`, and `decade-channel` sends it through `Channel::status(state, message)`. Hello carries a name, the verbs a client accepts, the kinds it shows and the pane it claims. Nothing in hello marks a client as an agent.

## Proposal

- Hello gains an optional `agent` block: `{"name": "coax", "version": "0.4.0", "session": "<id>"}`. A client without it is a plain pane program.
- A new `agent` message carries any subset of `state`, `activity` (what the agent is doing now), `question` (what it needs from Jack), `model`, `context` (`used` and `limit`), `tokens` (`input` and `output`) and `cost`. decade merges each update into what it already holds.
- An `ended` message says the session is over. A dropped socket does not.
- `status` folds into `agent` and goes. coax is its only user.
- `decade-channel`: `Channel::from_env` takes an optional `Agent` identity, `Channel::agent(update)` sends an update with only the fields set, and `Channel::ended()` ends the session. The crate is unreleased, so its Unreleased bullets are edited and its version stays.
- `docs/protocol.md` documents all of it.

The server keeps using the merged fields as it uses `status` today until the model issue lands.
close_reason: Landed in 896d419, with decade-code updated in decade-apps 4323017. coax still calls the removed Channel::status and is left to its own session.
